prompt:
CONCEPT: a citizen of the Carbon Nation, of the Graphite House. A female personification character with a wooden pencil with a graphite core, sharpened as her motif — the object reimagined as a woman in cloth and ornament that carry its materials, colors, shape and motifs. She does NOT hold, carry or wield the object; it is not a separate object. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.
ELEMENT TRAITS of Carbon (C) to carry in her design and the scene: two faces of one element: black soot and clear diamond; hexagonal lattices (graphite, graphene) as patterns, pencil-graphite grey, carbon-fibre weave; it bonds with everything and is the frame of all life. Palette: charcoal black, graphite grey, diamond white, a single living green.
HOUSE TRAITS of Graphite: silvery-grey pencil lead, flaking layered sheen, soft smudged shading. Palette: graphite grey, paper cream, cedar wood, black.
AGE: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
SILHOUETTE: lean and long-legged, with a natural neck length build; short cropped hair with no bangs, forehead bare; cedar-brown hair.
FACE — she must read as her own person at a glance, NOT the style's default pretty face and not a sister of the other characters: first impression — a warm, bright-eyed sweetness; olive skin; round face; moderately sized, realistically proportioned eyes — deep-set eyes, level outer eye corners; soft rounded brows; a small upturned nose shaped by soft shading; small bow lips; graphite-grey eyes; a dusting of freckles across nose and cheeks; semi-realistic game-illustration facial proportions, not a chibi or moe anime face.
WORLD — MECHA: year 2200, a city of graphene towers: hexagonal lattice facades, carbon-fibre weave surfaces, diamond-glass bridges. Her back unit carries two large sharpened-pencil-tip fins (a cedar-coloured cone with a graphite point), a pencil-tip crest rises from her headband, and cedar-wood-tone armor panels edge her plates. MECHA DESIGN: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. matte carbon-fibre weave armor with hexagonal lattice panels, diamond-clear visor and joint crystals, graphite-grey plates, a thin hexagonal halo. Her object leads the mecha design — its silhouette and parts must read at first glance in the plates, binders, helmet and back unit.
STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art — painterly semi-realistic rendering with soft volumetric light. Her face is modelled with gentle three-dimensional shading on the nose bridge, cheekbones, lips and jawline, drawn with thin soft-coloured contour lines instead of dark ink outlines; glossy layered hair with depth; she keeps her own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face. Even in a bright, high-key scene her face keeps soft form shadows. Crisp costume and prop detail, a vivid, readable silhouette and campaign-quality lighting. Not flat cel-shaded 2D anime, the image itself is not a sketch or line drawing, not photoreal.
EXPOSURE (bold): her outer layer (coat, cloak, robe or armor) stays on both shoulders, worn symmetrically; skin shows through the inner garment — a deep open neckline with natural cleavage, a fitted corset-like waist, slits where the form allows. The collar opens with the neckline in a V or folds down, never standing away from the neck. Nothing slipped off. Chest and pelvis covered; keep the costume WORLD describes, material and palette.
OUTPUT: one character image that works as card art. Vertical 2:3 frame, full body with head and feet inside the frame with clear margins, face turned toward the camera (front or three-quarter). Standing, card-ready pose; the environment may be rich while her design stays fully readable.
EXPRESSION: gaze angled down and away, slightly furrowed brow, lips lightly pressed or touched.
BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose or the frame.
ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no living creature, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (C) and atomic number (6) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.
ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, both hands drawn correctly as hands. No extra limbs.
